:::{.notes}

In EPI 203 and [our review of MLEs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#sec-intro-MLEs),
we learned how to fit outcome-only models of the form $p(X=x|\theta)$
to iid data $\vx = (x_1,…,x_n)$ using maximum likelihood estimation.

Now, we apply the same procedure to linear regression models:

:::

---

## Likelihood

$$
\ba
\Lik_i
&\eqdef p(Y_i=y_i|\vX_i = \vx_i)
&& \text{(conditional likelihood for observation } i\text{)}
\\
&= (2\pi\ss)^{-1/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2\ss}\eps_i^2}
&& \text{(Gaussian density evaluation)}
\\
\eps_i
&\eqdef y_i - \mu_i
&& \text{(definition of residual)}
\\
\mu_i
&\eqdef \mu(\vx_i)
&& \text{(conditional expectation function)}
\\
&= \vx_i \cdot \vb
&& \text{(linear predictor structure)}
\ea
$$

---

$$
\ba
\Lik
&\eqdef \Lik(\vy \mid \mx, \vb, \ss)
&& \text{(definition of joint likelihood)}
\\
&\eqdef \p(\vY = \vy \mid \mX = \mx)
&& \text{(definition via joint density)}
\\
&= \prodin \Lik_i
&& \text{(product over independent observations)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-linreg-lik}

---

## Log-likelihood

$$
\ba
\llik_i
&\eqdef \logf{\Lik_i}
&& \text{(definition of individual log-likelihood)}
\\
&= \logf{(2\pi\ss)^{-1/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2\ss}\eps_i^2}}
&& \text{(substitute individual density)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss} -\frac{1}{2\ss}\eps_i^2
&& \text{(logarithm product rule)}
\ea
$$

---

$$
\ba
\llik
&\eqdef \llik(\vy \mid \mx, \vb, \ss)
&& \text{(definition of total log-likelihood)}
\\
&\eqdef \logf{\Lik(\vy \mid \mx, \vb, \ss)}
&& \text{(logarithm of likelihood function)}
\\
&= \logf{\prodin\Lik_i}
&& \text{(substitute product likelihood)}
\\
&= \sumin\logf{\Lik_i}
&& \text{(logarithm of product is sum of logs)}
\\
&= \sumin \llik_i
&& \text{(substitute individual log-likelihood symbol)}
\\
&= \sumin \paren{-\frac{1}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss} -\frac{1}{2\ss}\eps_i^2}
&& \text{(substitute explicit log-likelihood form)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss} - \frac{1}{2\ss}\sumin \eps_i^2
&& \text{(distribute summation)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss} - \frac{1}{2\ss}\paren{\veps \cdot \veps}
&& \text{(express sum of squared residuals as dot product)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss} - \frac{1}{2\ss}\paren{(\vy - \vm) \cdot (\vy - \vm)}
&& \text{(substitute residual vector } \veps = \vy - \vm\text{)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss} - \frac{1}{2\ss}\paren{(\vy - \mX\vb) \cdot (\vy - \mX\vb)}
&& \text{(substitute mean vector } \vm = \mX\vb\text{)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss} - \frac{1}{2\ss}\sumin \paren{y_i - \paren{\vxi \cdot \vb}}^2
&& \text{(return to scalar summation form)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-linreg-loglik}

## Score function

$$
\ba
\mu_i'
&\eqdef \deriv{\vb} \mu_i
&& \text{(gradient of conditional mean w.r.t. } \vb\text{)}
\\
&= \deriv{\vb} \paren{\vx_i \cdot \vb}
&& \text{(substitute } \mu_i = \vx_i \cdot \vb\text{)}
\\
&= \paren{\deriv{\vb} \vb} \vx_i
&& \text{(apply matrix calculus rule)}
\\
&= \underbrace{\idmat}_{(p+1) \times (p+1)} \underbrace{\vx_i}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&& \text{(derivative of vector w.r.t. itself is identity matrix)}
\\
&= \underbrace{\vx_i}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&& \text{(identity matrix multiplication)}
\ea
$$

---

$$
\ba
\eps'_i
&\eqdef \deriv{\vb}\eps_i
&& \text{(gradient of residual w.r.t. } \vb\text{)}
\\
&= \deriv{\vb} (y_i - \mu_i)
&& \text{(substitute definition of residual)}
\\
&= \deriv{\vb} y_i - \deriv{\vb} \mu_i
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1} - \vx_i
&& \text{(outcome } y_i \text{ does not depend on } \vb\text{)}
\\
&= -\vx_i
&& \text{(subtract zero vector)}
\ea
$$

---

$$
\ba
\llik'_i
&\eqdef \deriv{\vb}\llik_i
&& \text{(individual score function w.r.t. } \vb\text{)}
\\
&= \deriv{\vb} \paren{-\frac{1}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss} -\frac{1}{2\ss}\eps_i^2}
&& \text{(substitute individual log-likelihood)}
\\
&= \deriv{\vb}\paren{-\frac{1}{2}\logf{2\pi\ss}} - \deriv{\vb}\frac{1}{2\ss}\eps_i^2
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1} - \frac{1}{2\ss}\deriv{\vb}\eps_i^2
&& \text{(constant term derivative vanishes)}
\\
&= - \frac{1}{2\ss} \cdot 2 \paren{\eps_i'} \eps_i
&& \text{(chain rule for scalar squared term)}
\\
&= - \frac{1}{\ss} \paren{-\vx_i \eps_i}
&& \text{(substitute } \eps_i' = -\vx_i\text{)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\ss} \vx_i \eps_i
&& \text{(simplify double negative)}
\ea
$$

---

$$
\ba
\ell'_{\vb}
&\eqdef \deriv{\vb}\ell
&& \text{(total log-likelihood score vector w.r.t. } \vb\text{)}
\\
&= \deriv{\vb} \sumin \llik_i
&& \text{(substitute total log-likelihood sum)}
\\
&= \sumin \deriv{\vb} \llik_i
&& \text{(exchange summation and derivative)}
\\
&= \sumin \llik_i'
&& \text{(substitute individual score symbol)}
\\
&= \sumin \frac{1}{\ss} \vx_i \eps_i
&& \text{(substitute individual score expression)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\ss} \sumin \vx_i \eps_i
&& \text{(factor out constant scalar } \frac{1}{\ss}\text{)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\ss} \underbrace{\tp{\mX}}_{(p+1) \times n} \underbrace{\veps}_{n \times 1}
&& \text{(matrix-vector formulation of the weighted sum)}
\ea
$$

## Solving the score equation

To find the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE),
we set the score vector equal to the zero vector.
The score equation for $\vb$ is:

$$
\ell'_{\vb} = \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
$$

Since $\ss > 0$, multiplying by $\ss$ gives the equivalent condition:

$$
\sumin \vx_i \eps_i = \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
$$

Substituting $\eps_i = y_i - (\vx_i \cdot \vb)$:

$$
\ba
\mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&= \sumin \vx_i \paren{y_i - (\vx_i \cdot \vb)}
&& \text{(substitute explicit residual expression)}
\\
&= \sumin \vx_i y_i - \sumin \vx_i (\vx_i \cdot \vb)
&& \text{(distribute summation across terms)}
\ea
$$

So the vector score equation becomes:

$$
\sumin \vx_i (\vx_i \cdot \vb) = \sumin \vx_i y_i
$$

Assume the design matrix $\mX$ has full column rank $p+1$.
This rank condition implies that $\sumin \vx_i \tp{\vx_i} = \tp{\mX}\mX$ is an invertible $(p+1) \times (p+1)$ matrix.
To solve for $\vb$, use the identity $\vx_i (\vx_i \cdot \vb) = (\vx_i \tp{\vx_i})\vb$:

$$
\ba
\paren{\sumin \vx_i \tp{\vx_i}}\vb
&= \sumin \vx_i y_i
&& \text{(factor out vector } \vb\text{)}
\\
\vb
&= \paren{\sumin \vx_i \tp{\vx_i}}^{-1}\sumin \vx_i y_i
&& \text{(multiply by inverse matrix)}
\\
\hvb
&= \paren{\underbrace{\tp{\mX}}_{(p+1) \times n} \underbrace{\mX}_{n \times (p+1)}}^{-1}
\underbrace{\tp{\mX}}_{(p+1) \times n} \underbrace{\vy}_{n \times 1}
&& \text{(matrix formulation of ordinary least squares / MLE vector)}
\ea
$$

---

## Hessian

$$
\ba
\llik_i''
&\eqdef \deriv{\tp{\vb}}\deriv{\vb} \llik_i
&& \text{(individual Hessian matrix definition)}
\\
&= \deriv{\tp{\vb}} \llik_i'
&& \text{(derivative of individual score vector)}
\\
&= \deriv{\tp{\vb}} \paren{\frac{1}{\ss} \vx_i \eps_i}
&& \text{(substitute individual score)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\ss} \vx_i \deriv{\tp{\vb}} \eps_i
&& \text{(factor out constant vector term } \vx_i\text{)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\ss} \vx_i (-\tp{\vx_i})
&& \text{(substitute transpose derivative } \deriv{\tp{\vb}}\eps_i = -\tp{\vx_i}\text{)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{\ss} \vx_i \tp{\vx_i}
&& \text{(simplify outer product term)}
\ea
$$

---

$$
\ba
\llik''
&\eqdef \deriv{\tp{\vb}}\deriv{\vb} \llik
&& \text{(total Hessian matrix definition)}
\\
&= \deriv{\tp{\vb}} \ell'
&& \text{(derivative of total score vector)}
\\
&= \deriv{\tp{\vb}} \sumin \llik_i'
&& \text{(substitute sum of individual scores)}
\\
&= \sumin \deriv{\tp{\vb}} \llik_i'
&& \text{(exchange summation and derivative)}
\\
&= \sumin \llik_i''
&& \text{(substitute individual Hessian symbol)}
\\
&= \sumin \paren{-\frac{1}{\ss} \vx_i \tp{\vx_i}}
&& \text{(substitute individual Hessian expression)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{\ss} \sumin \vx_i \tp{\vx_i}
&& \text{(factor out constant scalar } -\frac{1}{\ss}\text{)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{\ss} \underbrace{\tp{\mX}}_{(p+1) \times n} \underbrace{\mX}_{n \times (p+1)}
&& \text{(express summation as matrix product)}
\ea
$$

Expressed as a summation, the Hessian matrix is given by:

$$\hess = -\frac{1}{\ss} \sumin \vx_i \tp{\vx_i}$${#eq-lm-hess}

---

## Alternative approach using matrix derivatives

We can obtain the score function and Hessian directly in matrix-vector form without differentiating and summing term-by-term for each observation.

The total log-likelihood gradient with respect to $\vb$ is:

$$
\ba
\ell'_{\vb}(\vy \mid \mx, \vb, \ss)
&\eqdef \deriv{\vb}\llik(\vy \mid \mx, \vb, \ss)
&& \text{(definition of score vector)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\ss}\deriv{\vb}\paren{\sumin \paren{y_i - \paren{\vxi \cdot \vb}}^2}
&& \text{(substitute scalar sum of squares)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-linreg-score}

---

::: notes
Let's switch to matrix-vector notation:
:::

The sum of squared residuals can be rewritten in vector notation using the inner product:

$$
\sumin (y_i - \tp{\vx_i} \vb)^2 = (\vy - \mX\vb) \cdot (\vy - \mX\vb) = \tp{(\vy - \mX\vb)}(\vy - \mX\vb)
$$

---

Expanding this quadratic vector form gives:

$$
\ba
\tp{(\vy - \mX\vb)}(\vy - \mX\vb)
&= \paren{\tp{\vy} - \tp{\vb}\tp{\mX}}(\vy - \mX\vb)
&& \text{(transpose of difference)}
\\
&= \tp{\vy}\vy - \tp{\vb}\tp{\mX}\vy - \tp{\vy}\mX\vb + \tp{\vb}\tp{\mX}\mX\vb
&& \text{(expand matrix product)}
\\
&= \tp{\vy}\vy - 2\tp{\vy}\mX\vb + \tp{\vb}\tp{\mX}\mX\vb
&& \text{(combine scalar transpose terms } \tp{\vb}\tp{\mX}\vy = \tp{\vy}\mX\vb\text{)}
\ea
$$

---

::: notes
We will use some results from [vector calculus](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/vector-calculus.html):
:::

Differentiating each term in the expanded sum-of-squared-residuals quadratic form with respect to $\vb$:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vb}\paren{\sumin (y_i - \tp{\vx_i} \vb)^2}
&= \deriv{\vb} \tp{(\vy - \mX\vb)}(\vy - \mX\vb)
&& \text{(express in matrix vector form)}
\\
&= \deriv{\vb} \paren{\tp{\vy}\vy - 2\tp{\vy}\mX\vb + \tp{\vb}\tp{\mX}\mX\vb}
&& \text{(substitute expanded form)}
\\
&= \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1} - 2\tp{\mX}\vy + 2\tp{\mX}\mX\vb
&& \text{(matrix derivatives w.r.t. } \vb\text{)}
\\
&= -2\tp{\mX}(\vy - \mX\vb)
&& \text{(factor out } -2\tp{\mX}\text{)}
\\
&= -2\tp{\mX}(\vy - \E{\vY \mid \mX})
&& \text{(substitute conditional mean } \E{\vY \mid \mX} = \mX\vb\text{)}
\\
&= -2\tp{\mX} \veps
&& \text{(substitute residual vector } \veps = \vy - \mX\vb\text{)}
\ea
$${#eq-scorefun-linreg}

Multiplying the sum-of-squared-residuals gradient by the scalar factor $-\frac{1}{2\ss}$ yields the full log-likelihood score vector $\ell'_{\vb}$:

$$
\ba
\ell'_{\vb}
&= -\frac{1}{2\ss} \paren{-2\tp{\mX}\veps}
&& \text{(scale gradient by log-likelihood factor)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\ss}\tp{\mX}\veps
&& \text{(simplify factor } -\frac{1}{2\ss} \cdot (-2) = \frac{1}{\ss}\text{)}
\ea
$$

---

Setting the log-likelihood score vector equal to the zero vector:

$$
\ba
\mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&= \frac{1}{\ss}\tp{\mX}(\vy - \mX\vb)
&& \text{(set score vector to zero vector)}
\\
\mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&= \tp{\mX}(\vy - \mX\vb)
&& \text{(multiply by } \ss > 0\text{)}
\\
\mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&= \tp{\mX}\vy - \tp{\mX}\mX\vb
&& \text{(distribute } \tp{\mX} \text{ across difference)}
\\
\tp{\mX}\vy
&= \tp{\mX}\mX\vb
&& \text{(rearrange terms)}
\\
\hvb
&= (\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}\vy
&& \text{(multiply by inverse matrix } (\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\text{)}
\ea
$$

---

### Hessian

The Hessian (second derivative matrix) using matrix calculus is:

$$
\ba
\llik_{\vb, \tp{\vb}}''(\vy \mid \mx, \vb, \ss)
&\eqdef \deriv{\tp{\vb}} \paren{\frac{1}{\ss} \tp{\mX}(\vy - \mX\vb)}
&& \text{(differentiate score vector w.r.t. } \tp{\vb}\text{)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{\ss}\tp{\mX}\mX
&& \text{(matrix derivative of linear term w.r.t. } \tp{\vb}\text{)}
\ea
$$

The Hessian matrix $-\frac{1}{\ss}\tp{\mX}\mX$ is negative definite when $\mX$ has full column rank $p+1$, confirming that $\hvb = (\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}\vy$ uniquely maximizes the log-likelihood and is the maximum likelihood estimator for $\vb$.

---

Similarly (not shown):

$$
\es^2_{\text{ML}} = \frac{1}{n} \tp{(\vy - \mX\hvb)}(\vy - \mX\hvb)
$$
